text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout 'inference-service:v2' failing in eu-west-1 — several pods CrashLoopBackOff after node drain step. Alert group: infra-canary. thread_ts=2319876543

maya: I'm on this. Paging on-call now. Can someone share the canary rollout ID?

sam: rollout id `rollout-2026-03-15-1130` — started node drain and progressive canary (10%). First failures ~2 minutes after drain began.

ops-bot: PagerDuty triggered (PD:PD-8892) -> on-call: maya

maya: acked PD and joining. quick check: are we draining multiple nodes at once?

chris: yes, automated maintenance kicked off 2 nodes in eu-west-1 for kernel patches. They were staggered by 90s but both had pods for the canary.

lee: early hypothesis: HPA + drain interaction. HPA minReplicas=0 + aggressive downscale caused pods to be terminated during init, then restart ramp caused readiness flapping -> CrashLoopBackOff. Seeing init-container errors referencing `config-map:v2` missing.

maya: logs from one failing pod: ```
init container "fetch-config": error: configmap "inference-config-v2" not found
Stack: /app/init/fetch-config.sh:45
Exited with code 1
```

sam: that would explain it — new deploy expects updated configmap but node had stale kubelet cache? Or configmap not applied to cluster in time. Did the rollout include a configmap change?

chris: yes, configmap change was part of the release. It applied, but I’m seeing events where kube-apiserver returned 409 for configmap patchs during the canary window. Could be a write contention. Also HPA scaled down replicas to 0 while the init ran.

maya: customer impact? Tanya, what are we seeing from frontlines?

tanya: support telemetry: ~1.8% 5xx for EU customers hitting inference endpoints; most are 502/524 timeouts. Some customers reported degraded throughput; no complete outage. Marking as "partial degradation" for status page unless we fall back.

statusbot: STATUSPAGE: Created incident INC-231987 - "Investigating: Partial degradation for inference in eu-west-1"

maya: mitigation plan — immediate steps: 1) flip feature flag to avoid new code path 2) pause canary/rollback to prior revision 3) uncordon or stop further drains 4) update status. Who can flip the flag?

sam: I can flip flag. Doing API call now.

sam: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"inference-new-encoder","value":false}'` -> 200 OK. ops-bot: confirm.

ops-bot: feature flag `inference-new-encoder` set -> false by sam.

maya: good. Next rollback: sam/lee, can we do a quick rollout undo to previous stable revision?

lee: prepping rollback. Will pause the deployment and roll back to `inference-service:v1.9.8`

lee: running: ```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/inference-service --to-revision=134
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/inference-service
```

lee: rollback started. Observing pods spin up for v1.9.8 in canary pool.

sam: also running `kubectl uncordon` on node-zzz-12 and node-zzz-13 to stop further eviction storms: ```
kubectl uncordon node-zzz-12
kubectl uncordon node-zzz-13
```

chris: uncordon complete. Note: we should still finish kernel patch but schedule one node at a time and drain gently (grace period bump).

maya: monitoring metrics — error rates dropping?

tanya: support: error rate down to ~0.4% now, trending to baseline. Some customers still see increased latency for in-flight requests.

statusbot: STATUSPAGE: Updated INC-231987 -> "Partial degradation mitigated; rolling back to stable. Impacted region: eu-west-1."

lee: post-rollback check: verifying HPA and configmap correctness. HPA minReplicas set back to 2 for canary pool to prevent 0 -> 0 scaling during drains. Applying: ```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-service-hpa --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":2}]'
```

lee: patched HPA minReplicas=2. Confirmed.

sam: re-applied configmap v2 with a different name to avoid race: `inference-config-v2b` and updated rollout notes. We'll only deploy configmap first, wait 60s, then rollout.

chris: adding a pre-drain safety check to the maintenance automation: if any 5xx > 0.5% in region AND canary active -> abort drain. I'll open a PR for the automation.

maya: good. Customer comms — Tanya, please coordinate a short note: we rolled back and mitigated, minor impact to EU customers, root cause under investigation.

tanya: on it. Draft: "We experienced partial degradation for model inference in eu-west-1 during a canary deployment. We rolled back the release and mitigations are in place. Engineers are investigating the interplay between configmap application, HPA settings, and node drain automation. No ongoing impact expected." Will post in 10m.

maya: any outstanding actions for on-call? I'll hand off to lee for postmortem & follow-up. Lee, you own the postmortem and follow up with kernel/maintenance owners + platform for automation PR.

lee: taking handoff. I'll collect logs, timeline, and push the postmortem template. ETA initial draft in 6 hours.

maya: handing to lee. PD incident will remain open until postmortem links posted. Thanks team. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: Incident PD-8892 acknowledged by maya, assigned to lee for follow-up.

statusbot: STATUSPAGE: INC-231987 -> "Resolved / Monitoring" (updated by tanya)

maya: closing the live mitigation thread. Follow-up: postmortem, update canary runbook to include configmap-first deploy and HPA minReplicas guard, and automation change to abort drains during active canary with non-zero error rate.

lee: noted. Will link postmortem once ready.

sam: adding log snippets and `kubectl describe` output to the postmortem doc.

tanya: support to circle back to any affected enterprise customers who opened tickets.

chris: scheduling a brief sync with kernel/infra team to adjust maintenance window behavior.

maya: thanks all, back to normal ops. :white_check_mark:
